documents.title: Nurse/Midwife to Patient Ratios Policy
documents.scope: Only listed metropolitan wards at CAHS, EMHS, NMHS and SMHS; phased implementation.

sections.heading: 1–3.1: Applicability
sections.summary: Unlisted areas continue with Nursing Hours per Patient Day until their phase begins.

sections.heading: 3.2.2–3.3.2: Count eligible direct-care staff
sections.summary: Count direct-care RN, EN and midwives. Exclude AINs, supernumerary roles and the additional hands-free shift coordinator. Round required direct-care staff up.

sections.heading: 3.3.3: Skill mix
sections.summary: Clinical judgement determines the mix required for demand and acuity; this policy does not prescribe a universal senior-to-junior percentage.

sections.heading: 3.4.1: Ward-level coverage
sections.summary: Meet the ward-wide ratio on every shift; patient assignments within the ward may vary.

documents.title: Nurse/Midwife to Patient Ratios: Wards/Units in Scope for Implementation
documents.version: Schedule retrieved 19 September 2026; includes 23 February 2026 critical-care phase
documents.scope: Named wards only. PDF page numbers include cover; printed schedule pages differ.

sections.heading: Table 1: Listed medical/surgical wards
sections.summary: Listed wards require one nurse per four patients on AM/PM, plus one HFSC; night requires one per seven. Implementation dates vary by named ward.

sections.heading: Table 1: Listed critical-care wards
sections.summary: Listed ICU/NICU/paediatric critical-care areas use 1:1, or 1:2 for lower-acuity patients, plus HFSC each shift. Listed coronary-care areas use 1:2 AM/PM and 1:3 nights, plus HFSC.

documents.title: Management of Accrued Leave Policy
documents.scope: WA health entities; annual and long-service leave. Industrial instruments and law prevail.

sections.heading: 3: Accrued leave management
sections.summary: Subject to the applicable instrument, manage annual leave within two entitlements and take each long-service entitlement within two years, or three where allowed.

sections.heading: 3.2: Manager review
sections.summary: Before approval, consider balances, organisational priorities, holiday preferences, fairness, equity, financial impact and applicable industrial provisions. Agree leave timing with the employee.

sections.heading: 3.3–3.4: Workforce planning
sections.summary: Employees give sufficient notice; managers plan staffing and leave patterns for safe service delivery and periods of high demand.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.scope: WA health entities, including proposed AI uses, pilots and internally developed tools.

sections.heading: 3.1–3.4: Governance and assurance
sections.summary: Comply with the AI Standard, assign an accountable officer, perform required assessments before implementation and maintain ongoing monitoring and risk management.

sections.heading: 3.5: Workforce capability
sections.summary: Staff using or implementing AI must be appropriately informed, trained and qualified.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Standard
documents.scope: Mandatory supporting standard for AI use under MP 0193/25.

sections.heading: 8, Principle 2: Human-centred values
sections.summary: Humans retain control of healthcare and clinical decisions; AI supports clinicians who make final decisions.

sections.heading: 8, Principles 6–8: Explainability, contestability and accountability
sections.summary: Make AI use understandable, provide review mechanisms and preserve human oversight and accountability.

sections.heading: 8, Principle 1: Wellbeing
sections.summary: Document purpose, benefits, data, flaws and limitations; involve relevant stakeholders.

documents.title: WA Health System – ANF Nursing and Midwifery Industrial Agreement 2024
documents.scope: Registered nurses, midwives, enrolled mental-health and mothercraft nurses within agreement coverage.

sections.heading: 28(2): Ordinary hours
sections.summary: Average 38 hours weekly; ordinary roster arrangements can use 80 hours per fortnight with ADO accrual, or agreed alternatives. FTE and arrangement matter.

sections.heading: 28(11)–(12): Shift transitions
sections.summary: Night/day transitions require 20 hours free of duty; evening-to-day requires 9.5 hours. Clause 29 permits agreed flexible arrangements.

sections.heading: 28(14)–(15): Days off and duties
sections.summary: Two full days off weekly or four fortnightly. Normally at most seven consecutive duties and ten per fortnight; ten-hour nights have five/eight limits. Exceptions require review.

sections.heading: 30(4): Overtime rest
sections.summary: Overtime normally requires 9.5 hours between shifts, with specific release and penalty provisions.

sections.heading: 33(16)–(21): Taking annual leave
sections.summary: Annual leave can be taken in portions of at least one day by employer–employee agreement. Excess-leave provisions include a prior-denial exception.

sections.heading: 33(1)(b)-(e): Annual leave response and refusal
sections.summary: Respond within 14 days of submission. A refusal must be reasonable, written and explained within that time; specify any operational reasons.

documents.title: WA Health System – UWU Enrolled Nurses and Associated Staff Industrial Agreement 2024
documents.scope: Enrolled nurses, AINs, Aboriginal health workers/practitioners and ethnic health workers covered by the instrument.

sections.heading: 18.1: Ordinary hours
sections.summary: Average 38 hours weekly using specified cycles, including 76-hour or 80-hour fortnights with different ADO arrangements.

sections.heading: 20.4: Shift changes
sections.summary: Night/day transitions require 20 hours unless otherwise agreed. Evening-to-day requires 9.5 hours, with an eight-hour exception in country hospitals below regional level.

sections.heading: 41: Annual leave
sections.summary: This agreement has its own annual-leave provisions; do not apply ANF entitlements automatically to UWU-covered staff.

sections.heading: Instrument selection
sections.summary: The library separates nursing, medical, enrolled-nurse, public-service and salaried-officer agreements. Select the employee's actual instrument before applying conditions.

sections.heading: Mandatory frameworks
sections.summary: Frameworks group binding policies and define scope for local procedures. This index follows the user-specified staffing, leave and AI documents.

documents.title: WA Health System - Medical Practitioners - AMA Industrial Agreement 2024
documents.scope: Covered medical practitioners; excludes clinical academics and specified executive services under clause 3.

sections.heading: 34(11): Annual leave confirmation
sections.summary: Confirm in writing when annual leave may be taken within two weeks of receiving the written application.

sections.heading: 34(14): Annual leave staffing
sections.summary: Backfill for leave of two weeks or less requires urgent clinical/service grounds and delegated approval.

sections.heading: 34(13): Accrued annual leave
sections.summary: More than two years of accrued pro-rata entitlements triggers written notice to reduce leave within 12 months under an agreed plan.

sections.heading: 16(6): Doctors-in-training roster changes
sections.summary: Clinically appropriate mutual replacement requires Head of Department or nominee approval.

documents.title: Nursing and Midwifery Workforce Planning Framework
documents.scope: Planning guidance supporting service profiles; linked policy distinguishes this supporting information from mandatory related documents.

sections.heading: Introduction and service profiles
sections.summary: Minimum ratios do not cover all staffing needs. Local clinical judgement determines skill mix; service profiles address demand, acuity and additional roles.

sections.heading: Step 7: Allocate hours to service requirements
sections.summary: Roster allocation considers time, weekday, skill mix, seasonal variation, multidisciplinary availability and local service needs.

rules.restSource: Conditional: ANF 28(11)–(12), 30(4); UWU 20.4. No universal minimum inferred.

restRules.condition: ANF-covered staff, subject to approved clause 29 arrangements

ratios.scopeNote: Named ward and commencement date must match; add one HFSC beyond direct-care count.
Named ward and commencement date must match; assess clinical need for HFSC.

AMA_2024.action: Written confirmation of when leave can be taken; not automatic approval.

conditions: Seven consecutive duties is a where-practicable provision; an employee request and employer approval can permit more.
Five consecutive ten-hour nights has an employee-request/employer-approval exception.
Days off are consecutive where practicable; apply clause 28(14) night-shift sequencing.
Approved clause 29 flexible arrangements may vary methods; do not infer an exception without evidence.
Count whole days free from duty, including cross-midnight shifts; check roster history at fortnight edges.

excessLeaveAssessment.note: Two entitlements is not a universal fixed-hour threshold. Preserve the source-system excess calculation; do not silently recalculate with a generic weeks-to-hours conversion.

limitations: Roster service-unit codes are not mapped to the named hospital wards in the ratio schedule; do not claim policy-ratio compliance without that mapping and patient census.
Clinical acuity, competencies and HFSC/direct-care assignments are needed to confirm safe skill mix.
Ordinary-hours limits depend on agreement, FTE, ADO arrangement and approved local arrangements; 76 or 80 hours is not a universal legal maximum.
Index contains focused nursing, staffing, accrued-leave and AI provisions, not every policy or award in the statewide directories.
Supervisor approval and employee agreement remain workflow requirements; automated readiness is not final approval.
Page references are one-based PDF page numbers, including covers and registration orders.
Response deadlines above concern annual leave under the identified instrument; they do not imply automatic approval or apply universally to all leave types.
